messages.content: I have another museum trip to sort out. I need to be in St. Louis for a condition review Tuesday afternoon and an installation Wednesday that should wrap around 5:00. I’m leaving from Atlanta and traveling alone.

What dates are the Tuesday review and Wednesday installation, and what time does the review begin? I’ll compare arriving Monday evening with flying early Tuesday, then look at both Wednesday evening and Thursday morning returns.
The review is Tuesday, July 14 at 1:30 p.m., and installation is Wednesday, July 15. The museum says 5:00 p.m. is the expected finish, but that is not guaranteed.

I found two practical nonstop outbound choices from Atlanta. Delta leaves Monday, July 13 at 6:05 p.m. and reaches St. Louis at 6:43 p.m. local time for $238 round trip when paired with the Thursday return. Southwest has an early Tuesday flight leaving at 7:05 a.m. and arriving at 7:42 a.m.; its comparable round trip is $221. The museum is about 25 to 35 minutes from the airport in ordinary traffic, so the Tuesday flight leaves almost five hours before the review after allowing time to deplane and collect any checked case.
That early flight technically works. What happens if it is delayed or canceled? There is no flexibility on the review once the courier team starts.

That is the weakness of the Tuesday option. A delay of a few hours would consume the buffer, and a cancellation would leave few same-day recovery choices that arrive before 1:30. The Monday Delta flight has later backup departures that evening and gives you an overnight margin. It adds one hotel night, but it is substantially safer for the fixed museum commitment.
Agreed. Keep Monday as the likely outbound. Now compare the returns. I do not want to leave the museum early just to catch a flight.

For Wednesday, the last useful nonstop I found departs St. Louis at 7:10 p.m. and arrives in Atlanta at 9:42 p.m. To use it comfortably, you would want to leave the museum by about 5:15, and even then traffic or a slow handoff could make the airport timing tight. A later 8:35 p.m. itinerary connects in Nashville and reaches Atlanta at 12:20 a.m.; it gives more margin but still assumes the installation does not run much beyond 6:00. Thursday has a 7:20 a.m. nonstop arriving in Atlanta at 9:53 a.m. and a 9:45 a.m. nonstop arriving at 12:18 p.m.
How much more is the Thursday 9:45 return compared with trying for Wednesday night? Include the extra hotel night in the comparison, even if the hotel is only an estimate for now.

Using the Monday outbound, the Wednesday 7:10 p.m. nonstop prices at $204 round trip. The Thursday 9:45 a.m. pairing is $238, so the airfare difference is $34. A suitable hotel near the museum is likely to run about $175 to $215 including tax for Wednesday night. That puts the Thursday choice roughly $209 to $249 above the Wednesday nonstop overall. The connecting Wednesday itinerary is $267, making it $63 more than the Wednesday nonstop before any lodging difference.
The 7:10 sounds too exposed. Is the Thursday 7:20 flight meaningfully cheaper than 9:45?

Yes. Pairing Monday evening with the Thursday 7:20 a.m. nonstop is $219 round trip, which is $19 less than the 9:45 return. It would require leaving a museum-area hotel around 5:30 a.m. The later flight allows a more ordinary departure from the hotel but gets you back to Atlanta more than two hours later.
I can handle the early airport run. Before deciding, what are the fare and seat-selection differences on that $219 pairing?

The $219 fare is Delta Main Cabin. It includes standard seat selection at booking and permits changes without a change fee, though a fare difference can apply. Basic Economy is $179, but seat assignment is deferred and the ticket is more restrictive. The current Main Cabin seat map has window seats available on both flights, while the Basic Economy fare would not let you choose one now.
Use Main Cabin. For work flights, please keep a window seat as the first choice whenever seat selection is available.

Understood. For this pairing, 18A is open on the Monday outbound and 14A is open on the Thursday return. Both are standard Main Cabin window seats with no additional seat charge. I have not selected or held them because we are still comparing the itinerary.
Good. What is the actual schedule again, and how much buffer does Monday give me before Tuesday’s review?

The proposed outbound leaves Atlanta Monday, July 13 at 6:05 p.m. Eastern and arrives in St. Louis at 6:43 p.m. Central. Allowing 20 minutes to deplane and about 35 minutes to reach a hotel near the museum, you should be checked in around 7:40 p.m. The condition review begins at 1:30 p.m. Tuesday, so you would have the full morning plus roughly five hours after a normal breakfast before you need to report.
And on Thursday, is 5:30 early enough to leave the hotel if I have one checked equipment case?

It is workable but not generous. A 5:30 a.m. departure should reach the terminal around 6:00, about 80 minutes before the 7:20 flight. Delta’s checked-bag cutoff at St. Louis is 45 minutes before departure, leaving about 35 minutes of cushion. Leaving at 5:15 would provide a more comfortable margin, especially if the case needs any special handling.
Then assume a 5:15 hotel departure. I would rather have the extra margin. Does the Monday-to-Thursday plan mean three hotel nights?

Yes. The hotel search should cover check-in Monday, July 13 and check-out Thursday, July 16: three nights. That supports the Monday arrival, the Tuesday review, the full Wednesday installation, and the early Thursday airport run without forcing a rushed Wednesday departure.

That is the right anchor. Keep the Monday 6:05 outbound and Thursday 7:20 return, Main Cabin, with those window seats if they remain available. Do not book yet. Next time we can look for a hotel that is convenient to the museum and can arrange the early ride.

The working flight plan is Delta Main Cabin from Atlanta to St. Louis on Monday, July 13, departing at 6:05 p.m. and arriving at 6:43 p.m. local time, with the nonstop return Thursday, July 16 at 7:20 a.m., arriving in Atlanta at 9:53 a.m. The current round-trip fare is $219. Seats 18A outbound and 14A return are available window seats at no extra charge, but neither the flights nor seats have been held. This establishes hotel dates of July 13 through July 16 for three nights, with a planned 5:15 a.m. departure for the airport Thursday. The Wednesday evening options are set aside because the installation finish is uncertain.
